subject: Evidence export & residency: post-incident log hold and slicing request
messages:
From: Stella Ng <stella.ng@medisys.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medisys SecOps <secops@medisys.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Observed anomalous API usage — request for post-incident retention and evidence exports

Hi Aditya,

We observed anomalous activity that looks like automated scanning against our API keys provisioned to Redwood on 2026-12-01 between 23:10–23:46 UTC. Our team opened an internal investigation (HL-2026-998) and we need Redwood to preserve and export logs and related artifacts for forensic analysis. Specifically we need:

- Raw request logs (headers, body size, client IP if available) for 2026-12-01 22:30 UTC — 2026-12-02 01:00 UTC
- Any gateway or WAF events tied to the same API keys
- Chain-of-custody notes and a hash-based integrity check for exported files
- Confirmation of where logs will be stored (region / residency) and how long Redwood will hold them while the investigation is open

Can you confirm an expected ETA for a secure export and whether you can provide a short-form custody manifest? We may need the artifacts preserved beyond your default retention pending legal review.

Thanks,
Stella
Stella Ng
Security Incident Response
Medisys Inc.
stella.ng@medisys.com

Attachments: initial_alert_screenshot.png
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Stella Ng <stella.ng@medisys.com>
Cc: Medisys SecOps <secops@medisys.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:57:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed anomalous API usage — request for post-incident retention and evidence exports

Stella — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. We’ll treat this as a legal hold request and start preservation immediately. High-level plan (I will coordinate execution with Karthik and Soojin):

1) Snapshot: Take a forensics snapshot of request logs and relevant infra logs covering 2026-12-01 22:30 UTC to 2026-12-02 01:00 UTC. Snapshot will include request metadata (timestamp, path, method, response code), client IPs where logged, user-agent, and approximate payload size.
2) Storage & residency: We will place the snapshot into an encrypted, access-restricted bucket in us-central by default. If you require EU residency, we can make a copy to eu-west and maintain the EU copy under the same hold process — please confirm.
3) Integrity & chain of custody: Produce a manifest JSON with SHA-256 checksums for each artifact and record an internal chain-of-custody log.
4) Export delivery: Provide compressed JSONL (and a parquet summary for quick slicing) via a presigned S3 URL with a 72-hour window. We will also upload to a restricted Drive folder for your team.
5) Retention during investigation: We will hold the forensic snapshot for 180 days by default when a legal hold/reference is supplied; we can extend at your request.

ETA: initial snapshot + manifest within 36 hours, delivery of export + Drive link within 48 hours. If that timeline works, I’ll trigger the snapshot now and loop back with links and the custody template.

Any additional fields you need in the manifest (e.g., raw body captures, full request/response pairs) call that out and we’ll adjust scope.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observed anomalous API usage — request for post-incident retention and evidence exports

Quick technical notes to supplement Aditya’s plan:

- Retention tiers: our standard request logs are retained 30 days. For incidents with a submitted legal hold (like HL-2026-998) we create a frozen forensic snapshot and apply a 180-day hold by default; extensions can be requested by the customer’s legal or security teams.
- Snapshot contents: request metadata, internal routing traces (service IDs), and any available load-balancer logs. We do not store full request bodies by default for privacy; if you require bodies we can include them but will need your explicit approval and a data-minimization justification.
- Residency & duplication: primary snapshot will be in us-central (kms key: redwood-us-001). If you request EU residency for the copy, we will replicate to eu-west with the customer-managed key option. Replication will be logged in the custody manifest.
- Hashing & verification: all exported artifacts will be checksummed with SHA-256 and an HMAC-SHA256 using a rotation-limited key; the manifest will contain file size, checksum, creation timestamp, and signer.
- Access controls: exports are gated behind role-based access; we will provide a short access list for audit (who pulled the export and when).

I’m attaching a chain_of_custody_template.pdf with the fields we populate. I’ll prepare the snapshot job and hand it to Soojin for export.

-Karthik
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: chain_of_custody_template.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stella Ng <stella.ng@medisys.com>, Medisys SecOps <secops@medisys.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 15:02:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed anomalous API usage — request for post-incident retention and evidence exports

I’ve kicked off the snapshot job and verified the target time ranges. Implementation details:

- Export format: compressed JSONL for raw rows + partitioned parquet summary for quick queries. Filenames will be request_logs_20261201-20261202.jsonl.gz and request_logs_summary_20261201-20261202.parquet.gz.
- Storage & encryption: artifacts are in s3://redwood-forensics/us/medisys-inc/INC-2048/ and encrypted with KMS (redwood-us-001). Object ACLs are private; access will require a presigned URL or explicit IAM allow-list.
- Delivery & expiry: presigned URL sent to Stella will expire after 72 hours. If you need longer, we will extend and record the reason in the manifest.
- PII handling: by default we will redact sensitive PII fields (email contents, customer-supplied payloads) unless you request whole-body exports. Redaction schema is applied as an additional artifact to the export so your team can see what was removed.
- Integrity: generating SHA-256 + HMAC-SHA256 on each compressed file. Manifest (forensics_snapshot_manifest.json) will contain checksums, file sizes, and the chain_of_custody entries.

ETA update: snapshot finished; preparing compressed exports now. Expect presigned URL + Drive link within 12 hours.

Sooj
Incident Response Engineer
Redwood Inference
